title: Customer escalation war-room Acme Payments (P1): 2026-03-20 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Run a focused war-room with SRE, Serving Runtime, and Customer Success to get Acme Payments back to normal. This is a P1 customer-impact incident: payment authorization requests are failing intermittently (502/timeout) for ~30% of live traffic, started ~2026-03-20 02:15 UTC.

Goal for first 30 minutes:
- Stabilize traffic (reduce error rate to <1% or route to fallback model)
- Identify immediate root cause hypothesis and mitigation
- Agree on customer comms cadence and owner

Attendees (call):
- Avery Chen (owner, customer success)
- Diego Morales (on-call SRE, serving-runtime)
- Priya Singh (platform eng, routing & canary)
- Maya Lopez (solutions eng, Acme account lead)
- Samir Patel (support engineer, customer comms)
- Optional: On-call infra (pager) if we need infra-level remediation

Recent timeline (collected from logs/observability):
- 2026-03-20 02:12 UTC: small spike in 99th latency for model v2-base in us-west-2 pool
- 02:15 UTC: first customer error reports (Acme) - internal alert triggered (error rate >5% for 2m)
- 02:18 UTC: automated retry logic led to higher queueing -> increased 502s and some timeouts
- 02:25 UTC: serving-runtime autoscaler triggered new workers in us-west-2 but new workers saw high cold-start latency
- 02:32 UTC: traffic routing attempted fallback to v2-quant but some requests still failed (incompatible input shape observed in logs)

Impact summary:
- Customer: Acme Payments (production). ~30% of auth requests failing, user payments blocked, orders now backlog at merchant side.
- Business: P1 SLA breach potential, revenue and reputational risk.
- Scope: Affected region: us-west-2 dedicated pool for Acme (dedicated capacity). Other customers in same pool showing small uptick but not full failure yet.

Current hypothesis (top suspects):
1) Regression introduced in serving-runtime (recent PR 987) changes kernel selection causing inconsistent input handling for quantized variants; mismatch triggers shape/check errors for v2-quant fallback.
2) Autoscaler response/cold-starts + slow disk I/O for new workers -> queue growth and timeouts; retry logic amplifies failure.
3) Network partition between control-plane routing and dedicated pool leading to stale routing decisions.

Immediate mitigations to try now (ordered):
- (Diego) Temporarily route Acme traffic to hosted fallback pool (non-dedicated) that runs v2-base stable build. Action: update routing policy to prefer hosted while preserving stripe for non-critical endpoints. ETA: 10m.
- (Priya) Disable automatic retry escalation for Acme for next 30 minutes to avoid request amplification. Action: set retry multiplier to 0. ETA: 5m.
- (Maya + Diego) Roll back PR 987 on the us-west-2 serving-runtime nodes or pin model to previous compatible variant (v2-base non-quant). Action: deploy config pin. ETA: 20m if rollback needed.
- (Samir) Draft and send initial customer note acknowledging incident and expected timeline for next update (30m). Use tone: transparent, owning, ETA for mitigation.

Action items (owner / due / status):
- Diego Morales / 2026-03-20 02:40 UTC / in_progress: Implement routing to hosted fallback pool and monitor error rate.
- Priya Singh / 2026-03-20 02:30 UTC / done: Disable retry escalation for Acme (confirmed).
- Maya Lopez + Diego Morales / 2026-03-20 02:55 UTC / pending: Pin Acme routes to v2-base (non-quant) and roll back recent serving-runtime config if needed.
- Samir Patel / 2026-03-20 02:25 UTC / done: Initial customer acknowledgement sent (see comms draft below).
- Avery Chen / 2026-03-20 03:00 UTC / pending: Coordinate customer post-mitigation debrief and follow-up SLA credits if required.
- Diego Morales / 2026-03-20 03:15 UTC / pending: Collect and attach error traces and top N stack traces to the JIRA incident.

Draft customer message (short):
Hi Team Acme 
We’re currently investigating elevated errors affecting payment authorizations for your production traffic in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively working on a mitigation and we have temporarily routed traffic to a fallback pool to reduce impact. We’ll send another update in 30 minutes and share root-cause once confirmed. We apologize for the disruption.
 Avery (Redwood Inference)

Logs & quick checks (notes to SRE):
- Check kernel-selection logs around 02:00 02:25 for model v2 variants. Look for any "shape mismatch" or "input tensor size" failures.
- Check autoscaler events and disk I/O metrics for new worker provisioning.
- Confirm network health between control-plane and dedicated pool (latency, dropped connections).

Escalation policy reminder:
- If mitigation (routing to fallback) does not reduce errors to <1% within 15 minutes, escalate to infra on-call and product lead (cc: VP Product).
- If customer reports loss of orders or charge duplications, trigger legal/comms playbook.

Post-meeting follow-ups (to convert to confluence incident report):
- Owner: Diego  collate timeline + tracing artifacts and attach to JIRA-INC-2026-ACME-1234.
- Owner: Maya  write short postmortem draft focusing on autoscaler behavior and rollout gating for PR 987.
- Owner: Avery  coordinate customer debrief + credits discussion, share postmortem draft with Acme within 72 hours.

Notes / scratchpad (things to remember):
- We saw a similar issue in 2025-11 where quantized fallback caused unexpected shape checks; verify if same root cause.
- Keep canary rollback window open for 1 hour after stabilization.
- If we revert PR 987, need to fast-track patch with better input-shape checks before re-deploy.

Meeting adjourn: next check-in in 15 minutes (2026-03-20 02:40 UTC).
